assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about the idea of making every student do community service. I think students should not be forced to do it. Service is fine when a person picks it, though.

Some of my friends tutor little kids at the elementary school on Tuesdays. One of them told me a second grader finally read a hard word, and she said it was the highlight of her week. Another friend picks up trash by the creek behind our school. He says the creek looks different after he is done. They both signed up on their own, so they show up on time and do the work.

If the school makes it a rule, that will change. A lot of students already have jobs after school to pay for bills. Others watch their younger brothers and sisters, or they have practice and homework every night. I know kids who are really tired already, and a required number of hours would be one more thing on a long list. When people are forced, they usually do the bare minimum. They sign the sheet and leave early. That does not help anybody, and some kids will end up hating volunteering. It would be a problem for the school too, since teachers would have to check all the hours.

My idea is to make it easy to join. The school could have a sign-up table with local groups, run projects on weekends or at lunch, and read the names of volunteers at assemblies. More students would sign up if they were invited instead of pushed. I do not think a rule is needed for that.

Thank you for reading my letter.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I am writing to ask you to not make every student do community service. I think community service is a good thing and the school should encourage it, but I dont think it should be forced on people.

I have a few friends who tutor little kids at the elementary school and they really like it. One of them told me the best part of her week is when a second grader finally sounds out a hard word. Another friend picks up trash by the creek behind our school and he feels proud when he sees how much cleaner it is. It works for them because they picked it themselves. They actually care about the kids and the creek so they try hard.

If it was a requirement it would be different. Some of my friends work after school to help pay bills. Others have to watch their little brothers and sisters, or they have sports and homework. A required number of hours would just be one more thing in a day thats already full. When people are mad about an assignment they just do the least they can, like sign the sheet and leave early. That doesnt help anybody, and it might make them never want to volunteer again.

I think a better idea is to make service easy and fun. The school could set up a sign-up fair with different groups, have projects on weekends and at lunch, and give shout-outs to volunteers at assemblies. More kids would join if they felt invited instead of forced.

Thank you for reading my letter.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
